title: Scarce-skill rapid proof-of-impact: 14-day hire + onboarding playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is intended for hiring managers and People Ops when recruiting for rare/critical skills (e.g., compiler-level ML inference optimization, device driver expertise, exotic quantization experience) where time-to-impact and candidate bandwidth are constrained. Goal: get a new hire to demonstrate a concrete technical contribution in 14 calendar days and reach productive onboarding milestones by day 21.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target roles: senior ICs, short-window contractor-to-perm pilots, or ICs joining a small pod where one person is a single point of technical capability.
- Candidate availability: often part-time during notice period; assessments must be short and asynchronous-friendly.
- Hiring velocity prioritized over exhaustive process, but with calibrated checks for quality and inclusivity.

High-level timeline (14-day proof window + follow-on 7-day embed):
Day -7 to 0 (offer & preboarding):
  - Send a short preboarding packet: repo access request form, dev machine checklist, Slack invites to pod channel, short reading list (1–2 docs).
  - Confirm first-week mentor and pairing schedule.
  - Assign initial issue stub (very small, scoped) to set up dev environment early.

Day 0–3: orientation + environment setup
  - Day 0: quick sync (30m) with manager, mentor, and one stakeholder. Set expectations: 14-day deliverable described, definitions of done, and acceptance criteria.
  - Verify access to repo, CI, datasets, and test infra.
  - Confirm local run of a minimal end-to-end example.

Day 4–10: focused engineering sprint (candidate picks one path)
  Option A: Live small scoping issue (preferred when candidate is onsite or can pair)
    - 2–4 hour pairing session with mentor to scope fix/feature.
    - Candidate implements, writes tests, and opens a draft PR by day 7.
  Option B: Asynchronous micro-project (preferred when candidate limited time)
    - Deliverable: a short artifact (patch + README, or small benchmark) taking ~8–12 hours total.
    - Must include reproduction instructions and a short failure-mode note.

Day 11–14: review, iteration, and demo
  - Technical review within 48 hours of PR submission.
  - Candidate presents a 15-minute demo to pod + people-ops (recorded).
  - Outcome decisions: accept as-is (satisfactory), request small follow-up (<=3 days), or fail to meet acceptance (rare; fallback below).

Interview & evaluation rubric (calibrated for scarce-skill fast track)
Scoring: 1–4 scale (1 = insufficient, 2 = below bar, 3 = meets expectations, 4 = exceeds expectations). All interviewer notes must map to rubric categories and cite evidence.

Categories (weighting in parentheses):
  - Technical correctness & safety (30%): correctness of approach, reasoning about edge cases, test coverage.
  - Architecture & tradeoffs (20%): can explain design tradeoffs, constraints, and performance implications.
  - Debugging & reproducibility (15%): ability to produce reproducible results, debug pipeline failures, describe root cause.
  - Communication & asynchronous collaboration (15%): clarity of README/PR notes, responsiveness in async threads, concise demo.
  - Culture fit & ownership (10%): curiosity, follow-up, ability to receive feedback.
  - Security/legal awareness (10%): awareness of data handling, export restrictions, licensing where relevant.

Interviewer guidance (quick do/don't):
  - DO map every observed behavior to rubric categories and capture a one-line evidence item.
  - DO rate conservatively; for fast tracks, prefer 3+ for hire unless multiple independent reviewers score 2.
  - DO prioritize reproducible artifacts over long design essays.
  - DON’T conflate familiarity with a specific vendor/tool with domain competence.

Take-home micro-project rules (if used):
  - Timebox: estimate 8–12 hours. Communicate that in the assignment.
  - Provide a minimal scaffold: small repo with data subset, baseline script, and expected output format.
  - Acceptance criteria: clear pass/fail tests or benchmark target plus a short writeup (max 1 page).
  - Plagiarism: candidates may reference public code but must mark sources. Candidates must sign a brief honor statement.

Onboarding checklist (first 21 days)
First 24–72 hours:
  - Manager 30m: role context, expectations, org mapping, IP/security reminders.
  - Mentor 1-hour pair: walk through local dev reproducible example.
  - Setup: machines, VPN, KMS access, SSH keys, CI tokens.
  - Communication: join core Slack channels, calendar blocks for focus time, link to on-call rotation if applicable.

Day 4–14 (14-day proof window):
  - Daily 30m pairing/check-in (can be batched to fewer but longer blocks for part-time folks).
  - Engineering deliverable: assigned micro-project with acceptance criteria.
  - Weekly check: manager + mentor sync at day 7 and day 14 to assess risk and feedback.

Day 15–21 (embed):
  - Expand scope to a follow-on task that connects the 14-day deliverable to product or infra (e.g., integrate fix into main benchmark job).
  - Documentation: short postmortem / how-it-works doc (1–2 pages) authored by new hire.
  - Knowledge transfer: recorded 20–30 minute walkthrough for future hires.
  - Performance checkpoint: manager makes hire/permanent conversion recommendation by day 21.

Mentor & reviewer playbook
  - Mentor responsibilities: clear acceptance criteria, daily short feedback, unblocker ownership for infra issues, and sign-off on reproducibility.
  - Reviewer responsibilities: fast review turnaround (48 hours), leave actionable comments keyed to rubric, and attend final demo.
  - Conflict escalation: if reviewer and mentor disagree, convene manager + senior tech lead and use evidence log to adjudicate.

Templates (copyable)
  - Day 0 expectations email (one paragraph): outlines 14-day deliverable, pairing expectations, and access links.
  - Proof-of-impact acceptance checklist: reproducible run (yes/no), tests included (yes/no), perf regression (improved/neutral/worse), README present (yes/no), demo recorded (yes/no).
  - Debrief questions for candidate: what surprised you, edge cases you worried about, how would you productionize this, next 3 improvements?

Risk mitigation & fallback paths
  - If the candidate cannot produce by day 14 due to infra blocks: pause the clock for days lost if mentor confirms block and gives alternative microtask to demonstrate skill.
  - If deliverable is marginal: extend 3-day repair window with clear, limited scope tasks.
  - If candidate fails acceptance and still promising: offer a paid, short-term contractor pilot (2–4 week) with narrower acceptance criteria.
  - If candidate is not a fit: capture structured feedback for candidate and hiring process improvements; anonymize any sensitive notes.

Equity, accessibility, and inclusivity notes
  - Provide multiple ways to demonstrate skill (pairing, recorded demo, or written micro-project).
  - Timebox assignments and be explicit about expected hours.
  - Offer to provide accessible formats for any materials (e.g., transcripts for recordings).
  - Ensure debrief and scoring use objective evidence only; avoid subjective shorthand (e.g., "looks senior").

Postmortem & continuous improvement (people-ops responsibilities)
  - After each rapid-hire, People Ops runs a 1-hour retrospective with hiring manager and mentor to surface process failure modes and update playbook.
  - Maintain an evidence log template for calibration across hiring managers.

Appendix: quick checklists (copy/paste)
  - Preboarding packet items: HR forms, AUP, KMS request, repo access template, reading list (1–2 docs).
  - Minimal reproducibility checklist: seed, dataset subset, run commands, expected artifacts, CI job link.
  - Demo checklist: 15-minute demo, 5 minutes Q&A, recording link, acceptance checklist attached.

Notes and open questions (for iteration):
  - Pilot metric suggestions: time-to-first-merged-PR, time-to-first-benchmark-improvement, new-hire NPS after 21 days.
  - Consider building a small "rapid-hire infra" sandbox with zero-touch access for this program to reduce blocker risk.
